 BALTIMORE COUNTY, Md. (WBFF) — Julian Jones is switching in his councilman hat for his new role as county executive for Baltimore County after beating Republican Patrick Dyer in the 2026 general election.
 Jones is set to be the county’s first Black county executive.
 Jones has served on the Baltimore County Council since being elected in 2014. According to his campaign website, Jones became the first person elected as council chairman three consecutive times — and four times overall.
 Jones was the first Black lieutenant, captain, battalion chief and division chief in the history of the Anne Arundel County Fire Department.
 His priorities include safe communities, education and career readiness, jobs and the economy as well as energy affordability.
 Jones has delivered results for the county, including passing comprehensive police reform to strengthen training, improve use-of-force standards and increase transparency, creating the College Promise Program, which makes community college tuition free for Baltimore County students, passing the HOME Act to prevent discrimination against renters using housing vouchers and established an Office of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion to create fairness across government.
 Jones has also been outspoken about making juveniles accountable when they commit crimes.
 “Well, first of all, we're going to continue to make sure we fund our police department with adequate funding, so that they can have the tools and resources to go after these individuals. Then number two, we're going to make sure that our state's attorney knows that we would hope that people would be held accountable,” Jones previously told FOX45 News in September after three teens were charged as adults in a Towson armed carjacking case.
 Jones will start his four-year term as county executive on Jan. 1, 2027.
